title: Broach Press
pages: Craft the controller with four sticky pistons, one redstone block at the bottom centre, one Limit Switch at the top centre, one Ribbed Machine Bed at the middle-left, one Tool Steel Stock at the middle-right, and one Hydraulic Cylinder in the center. The Limit Switch is the ram's end-of-travel and guard interlock: like an interlocked press gate, the control circuit does not start a stroke unless the actuator is tripped. Craft two Limit Switches from a lever (actuator arm) on top, two copper ingots (forge:ingots/copper, snap contacts) beside one redstone dust, and three Sealed Steel Plates as the sealed body. A plain redstone block or a bare lever cannot replace it; switching distance and repeatability are not simulated. Make the cylinder with four Sealed Steel Plates, two sticky pistons, one Tool Steel Stock, one Lubricating Oil and one Pressure Gasket. Clamp four slime balls to obtain the gasket; press eight forge:seeds for oil. Craft the Ribbed Machine Bed from four kiln-fired Tool Steel Stocks at the corners, two Sealed Steel Plates across its rails, two Press-stamped Tab Lock Washers at the sides and a Lubricating Oil charge in the centre. The heavy bed resists the broach ram, while the lock washers secure its cross ribs; unbraced stock and loose iron nuggets cannot replace it. JEI shows the craft and its ingredients. The assembled ram and seal make this press distinct from a bare piston; grease and raw slime cannot substitute. The craft consumes an oil item as a sealed charge; the machine does not simulate fluid pressure or a refill cycle.

A broach is a cutting tool, so its ram needs a harder, more wear-resistant steel than plain tempered steel: shapelessly combine four steel billets with one chromium ingot and one vanadium ingot (tags forge:ingots/chromium and forge:ingots/vanadium) into four Tool Steel Charges, then fire each charge in the Kiln at 900 heat for 140 ticks. Chromium and vanadium form hard carbides in the steel; plain tempered steel, a bare billet or an iron ingot are rejected in this slot. The charges can be hopper-fed into the Kiln like any firing input.

Put a redstone block directly to its north and an emerald block directly to its south. Face sticky pistons inward above and below it. At controller height, place iron bars at all four diagonal corners beside the redstone and emerald anchors; these braces bind the two anchor beams while the cardinal east and west sides stay open. Above the north and south anchors put iron blocks, then join each to the vertical ram with iron bars at the four upper corners. This crown holds the long broach path aligned; missing either iron block or upper tie stops the press. The projector shows all fourteen surrounding parts. This is the first t2 press to anchor on the horizontal north/south axis with vertical pistons instead of a vertical base/lid with horizontal pistons. Right-click the controller with feedstock from a loaded broaching recipe. The press loads one recipe batch into its stock buffer, processes it over 40 ticks, and holds the output for empty-hand collection or bottom-face extraction. A missing redstone or emerald anchor, a missing corner brace or crown part, or an outward/missing above/below piston stops operation. Restore the part to reform the press; adjacent presses cannot share a brace.

The 23 exclusive JEI broaching recipes include six feedstocks for Broached Pins and three progression cuts: Bearing Steel Stock to Guide Rail Blank, Tool Steel Stock to two Shaft Keys, and two Tempered Copper Sheets to a Copper Busbar. Fourteen additional rows cut or compact distinct useful products. Iron and gold nuggets become full ingots at nine per batch; three copper ingots form a lightning rod; four gold ingots form golden horse armor. Amethyst, coal, diamond, emerald, lapis, netherite, quartz, and raw copper, gold and iron can be packed into their respective blocks at the listed material costs. These storage rows help a hopper line buffer bulk feedstock without a crafting table. JEI gives each batch size. The press is hand-fed or accepts stock through configured input faces, has no FE port, and holds its output for extraction.

Broached pins are electrical-tier parts: two of them form the bottom corners of the Arc Press controller, beside a copper ingot, under a copper/conductive crystal/copper row and two Porcelain Insulators around an iridium ingot. Keep the Broach Press after the Press; the Resonance Infuser cannot be reached without its pins. A bare chain does not substitute for a pin.

Automation: place a hopper or item pipe against any input face (all faces except the bottom by default) and feed a loaded recipe input. A formed controller processes one batch every 40 ticks without FE; its bottom face outputs to a hopper or pipe. Empty-hand right-click collects buffered products. Sneak-right-click a face with an empty hand cycles it through input, output and off. Full output pauses processing; broken or unloaded structures do not process. Buffered items and side settings survive saving; breaking the controller drops its buffers.
